corePages.headline: Die V2-Regel
corePages.bodyGerman:
Ich (1) komme (2) aus Deutschland.
Heute (1) wohne (2) ich in Berlin.
Morgen (1) lerne (2) ich Deutsch.
corePages.bodyEnglish: In every German statement the conjugated verb is the SECOND element — no matter what fills position 1. Move a time word to the front and the subject slides behind the verb. This is the single most important rule in basic German.
corePages.culturalTip: 'Heute ich lerne' is the classic learner mistake. Time first → verb second → subject third: 'Heute lerne ich'.

corePages.headline: Fragen bauen
corePages.bodyGerman:
Kommen (1) Sie (2) aus Deutschland?   →  Ja.
Woher (1) kommen (2) Sie?              →  Aus Indien.
corePages.bodyEnglish: Yes/No question: verb takes position 1. W-question (Woher, Wo, Wie, Was): question word is position 1, verb stays position 2. Same V2 skeleton, different occupant of slot 1.

corePages.headline: Orte & Länder
corePages.bodyEnglish: 'kommen aus' = you originate there. 'wohnen in' = you live there. Both fixed phrases — learn them as chunks.

grammar.ruleHeadline: Das Verb steht immer an Position 2!
grammar.explanationEnglish: German word order is verb-second (V2). Count elements, not words: whatever you put first, the conjugated verb follows immediately, and the subject usually finishes the clause.
grammar.englishBridge: English: 'Today I go to school.' → German flips it: 'Heute GEHE ich zur Schule.' The verb still owns slot 2 — the subject just moved after it.
grammar.commonMistake: Don't translate English order directly: 'Heute ich gehe' ✗ → 'Heute gehe ich' ✓
grammar.targetSentenceGerman: Ich komme aus Deutschland und wohne in Berlin.
grammar.targetSentenceEnglish: I come from Germany and live in Berlin.

writing.promptEnglish: Build: 'Morgen lerne ich Deutsch mit Maria.'

practice.explanationEnglish: V2: subject (1), verb (2), then the rest. 'komme' must be second.
Formal 'Sie' always takes the -en ending: 'wohnen Sie'.
Yes/No questions put the verb in position 1: verb + Sie + rest.
